clue.text: Boy nurses poorly bat

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the first piece cradles the second inside it

parts.note: 'Boy!' as an exclamation of surprise means wow
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A lad is looking after a sick bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' reads as a child but is the exclamation 'Boy!', and the bat is a cricket bat, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are traditionally made from the timber of a particular tree, so the tree's name stands for the bat.

clue.text: Photographer latterly inside pans dance studio

indicators.note: inside means put the photographer's letter into the pans

parts.note: woks are Chinese cooking pans

indicators.note: latterly means take the last letter

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A photographer's work ends up inside a dance studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or building where things are made or work is done.

clue.text: Joiner's brave wearing bandage

indicators.note: the bandage wears the brave word, so it wraps around it

parts.note: lint is a dressing for wounds
game means willing and brave

explanation.surface: A carpenter bravely wears a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter but means something that joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of tissue that connects bones, so it is literally a joiner.

clue.text: Adviser's contributing line to ancient poet failing to start

indicators.note: contributing a letter means it is put into the poet's name
failing to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Horace was a Roman poet

explanation.surface: An adviser contributes lines to an old poet who can't get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' cuts HORACE to ORACE, and 'contributing' puts L in.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient priest or shrine that gave counsel from the gods; now any wise counsellor.

clue.text: Wrong lock used to secure health centre

indicators.note: the first piece is used to hold the second, so it wraps round it

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A mistaken lock was fitted to keep a health centre safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong or sin, as in 'forgive us our trespasses', is a transgression.

clue.text: Underdone cheese dish not chewed

indicators.note: not means remove the chewed word from the dish

parts.note: rarebit is Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast
bit is the past tense of bite

explanation.surface: An undercooked cheese dish was left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked lightly so it is still red inside.

clue.text: Maritime plant providing booster in county

indicators.note: in means the booster goes inside the county

parts.note: shire is an English county
an amp is an amplifier, a booster of sound

explanation.surface: A coastal plant is used as a pick-me-up in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Shire is a traditional English word for a county.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible plant growing on sea cliffs and salt marshes.

clue.text: Beauty queen avoids kebab when among high-class society

indicators.note: among means the trimmed kebab goes inside the high-class letters

parts.note: A1 is first-rate, high-class

indicators.note: avoids means the queen letters are left out

parts.note: a doner is a kebab of spit-roasted meat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A beauty queen turns down a kebab while mixing with posh society.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means top quality; written AI here. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome youth loved by Aphrodite, whose name stands for any beautiful man.

clue.text: Dwarf plant getting shelter inside

indicators.note: inside means the shelter goes in the plant word

parts.note: a plant is a planted spy
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A small plant is kept under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests greenery but is an undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White fairy tale.

clue.text: Newspaper gossip read over salad

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

indicators.note: to read something over can mean turning it over, so the word for gossip is written backwards

parts.note: gab is chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Someone reads the newspaper's tittle-tattle over a lunchtime salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad in its figurative sense is a confused mixture, as is a jumbled collection.

clue.text: One's blown millions pursuing stardom, regularly revealing part of body

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so M follows the letters picked from stardom
regularly means take every other letter of stardom

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
a bone is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone squandered millions chasing fame and ended up exposing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'stardom', T, R, O; 'revealing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument is something a player blows into.

clue.text: Religious school fills in register with electronic tablet

indicators.note: fills in means the religious school is inside the register

parts.note: a log is a register or record
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A religious school fills in its register on a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablet' suggests a computer but means a medicinal sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal sweet, a tablet sucked for a sore throat.

clue.text: When retiring, not one left fruit wine

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: not one means no
limes are a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A wine buff complains that no fruit was left in the wine on retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses the whole run NO L LIMES, giving NOLLIMES backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A white grape variety and the white wine made from it, notably in Bordeaux and Australia.

clue.text: School member who gets bullied?

parts.note: a school is also a shoal of fish or crustaceans, and a small weak child is called by the same name as one of these sea creatures

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a weedy pupil picked on in the playground; the other reading is a creature in a school of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crustacean that swims in schools, and slang for a puny person likely to be picked on.

clue.text: Not middling grubber delivered into cricket wicket causes irritation?

indicators.note: delivered into means put inside

parts.note: a chain is 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch

indicators.note: not middling means the middle is left out, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A low ball bowled into a cricket wicket causes irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: A grubber is a ball rolling along the ground; 'Not middling' leaves GR, 'delivered into' CHAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation from disappointment or humiliation.

clue.text: What farmer hears coming from radio in kitchen?

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farmer hears a noise from the radio left on in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunting noise a pig makes, which a farmer would hear in the sty.

clue.text: Cricket side that's played in headwear

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
a horn is an instrument that is played

explanation.surface: A cricket team performs wearing hats.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leghorn is a straw hat made from plaited Italian wheat straw, named after the city of Livorno.

clue.text: Crowd gathering in east mostly like a certain US writer

parts.note: jam is a crowd or crush

indicators.note: gathering means the letters gather into a new order
mostly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts IN EAST to INEAS, and 'gathering' rearranges it to ESIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the style of Henry James, the American-born novelist.

clue.text: Will from church avoids payment, as vessel goes round

indicators.note: goes round means the vessel encloses the rest

parts.note: a bath is a vessel for bathing

indicators.note: avoids means the church letters are left out

parts.note: a cheque is a payment

explanation.surface: A will leaves a church avoiding payment as a vessel is passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a noun but is the verb, leaving something in a testament; 'from' and 'as' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something in a testament.

clue.text: Athlete they copy, moving second to first

indicators.note: moving means a letter is moved
to first means the moved letter goes to the front

parts.note: printers copy text

explanation.surface: Athletes copy each other moving from second to first.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an athlete who specialises in short fast races such as the hundred metres.

clue.text: Head off excited into Norwich's outskirts after seeing museum's artist

indicators.note: after says the rest comes behind the museum's letters

parts.note: V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: into puts the trimmed word inside the outer letters
outskirts means the first and last letters of Norwich
head off means remove the first letter

parts.note: agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: Someone excited heads into the edge of Norwich to see a famous painter after a museum visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' trims AGOG to GOG, which goes 'into' N...H, the 'outskirts' of Norwich.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch post-impressionist painter of Sunflowers and The Starry Night.

clue.text: Scoff endlessly before parking vehicle

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to scoff is to jeer
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone eats greedily without stopping before parking the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like eating but means mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugged four-wheel-drive car first built for the US military.

clue.text: Clergyman joins walkers in search

indicators.note: joins ... in means the clergyman goes into the walkers
joins ... in means the clergyman goes into the walkers

parts.note: feet are walkers
RR is Right Reverend

explanation.surface: A clergyman joins walkers in a search.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret out is to search thoroughly.

clue.text: Musicians start to study scale (not new)

indicators.note: start to means the first letter
not new means the N for new is removed

parts.note: extent is scale

explanation.surface: Musicians start to study scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of six musicians.

clue.text: Leaning six-footer circumvents lowest of ceilings, note

indicators.note: circumvents means goes round

parts.note: an ant has six legs

indicators.note: lowest of means the last letter in a down clue

parts.note: la is a note of the scale

explanation.surface: A tall person ducks under a low ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something set at a slant is tilted, leaning away from upright.

clue.text: Football team originally called back, as foreign brass introduced

indicators.note: introduced means put inside the reversed word
called back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: nee (French for born) introduces a woman's original surname
brass is slang for money, and the lev is Bulgaria's currency

explanation.surface: A football club, called back as a foreign coach is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NEE to EEN; brass is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields this number of players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: River's island seen on the turn into motorway

indicators.note: into puts the island-and-sour pieces inside the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway
milk on the turn is going sour

explanation.surface: A river island is spotted turning round beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway running north from London; 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A major tributary of the Mississippi in the US.

clue.text: Approve assistant bodyguard

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
SS was Hitler's bodyguard

explanation.surface: An assistant approves a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve a law is to pass it.

clue.text: Dramatist's giant novel available at back of shop

indicators.note: the anagram sits behind the word for shop

parts.note: to shop someone is to inform on them, to rat

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A huge novel is on sale at the back of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a store but is the British verb for betraying someone; 'available' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was the English playwright of The Winslow Boy and Separate Tables.

clue.text: Used to model clothes against an academic

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means dresses or covers, so the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: an artist's model sat for the painting
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A scholar was once used to model clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning dresses or wraps; an artist's model sits, so 'Used to model' gives the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person, especially one with deep knowledge of a field.

clue.text: Phoebe, say, crossing over street,inhales French cigarettes untipped?

indicators.note: inhales means the street letters take in the cigarette letters
over signals the street abbreviation is turned back to front
untipped means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Gitanes is a French cigarette brand

explanation.surface: Phoebe crosses the street smoking strong French cigarettes without filters.
explanation.walkthrough: Gitanes are strong French cigarettes; 'untipped' drops their first letter, and 'crossing over' turns the street abbreviation to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Phoebe was one of the female Titans, daughters of Uranus and Gaia.

clue.text: One sharply scores three after moving around clubs

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the clubs letter
after moving means the letters of three are rearranged

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer scores three after moving round the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after moving' rearranges THREE to ETHER, which goes 'around' C.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver cuts lines into metal with a sharp tool and acid.
